name: H7 flight controller, 30.5 mm
summary: A 30.5 mm flight controller with an H7-class processor, dual IMUs and a barometer. Sample data: the supplier and every figure here are fictional.

evidence.summary: Supplier datasheet, pinout and major-component BOM received.
checked: Pinout and ratings as stated by the supplier
Major components listed in the supplier BOM

Bill of materials for TM-FCT-H7-30 (major components)

evidence.summary: One sample inspected and component markings compared with the supplier BOM.
checked: Markings on the processor, both IMUs and the barometer match the supplier BOM
notChecked: Whether the chips are genuine, beyond markings

parts.name: Circuit board
parts.role: Connect every sensor, the processor and the outputs on one board.
parts.whatItDoes: A six or eight layer board with a 30.5 mm square mounting pattern. Power regulators, sensors and the processor share it.
parts.whyItMatters: Layout decides how much motor noise reaches the sensors. Two boards with the same chips can fly very differently.
buyingChecks: Ask for the layer count and whether the IMU has its own regulator
Check the mounting pattern matches your frame
Ask whether the board is conformal coated

parts.name: Processor
parts.role: Runs the autopilot software and the control loop.
parts.whatItDoes: A fast 32-bit processor reads every sensor, works out how the aircraft is moving, and sends a new command to each motor many times a second.
parts.whyItMatters: Processor headroom decides which autopilot software you can run and how many features you can enable at once.
buyingChecks: Check the board has a supported target in your autopilot software
Ask how the supplier sources processors, and from which distributor
Ask whether a processor change would be announced before shipping

parts.name: Inertial sensors (IMUs)
parts.role: Measure rotation and acceleration so the aircraft knows how it is moving.
parts.whatItDoes: Two separate gyroscope and accelerometer chips. Using two lets the autopilot compare them and keep flying if one fails or reads badly.
parts.whyItMatters: Sensor noise and vibration isolation set how stable the aircraft is. They are also where remarked or substituted chips most often appear.
buyingChecks: Check the IMU models against your autopilot's supported list
Ask whether the IMUs are soft-mounted or on the main board
Ask for markings photos from each batch

parts.name: Barometer
parts.role: Measures air pressure to estimate altitude.
parts.whatItDoes: A small pressure sensor that lets the autopilot hold height. It is usually covered with foam to block wind from the propellers.
parts.whyItMatters: A noisy or uncovered barometer makes altitude hold drift, which matters for inspection and mapping work.
buyingChecks: Check the barometer has a foam cover
Check the model is supported by your autopilot
Keep it away from direct propeller wash when mounting

parts.name: Connectors
parts.role: Plug in receivers, GNSS, cameras and ESCs.
parts.whatItDoes: Small locking JST-GH connectors along the board edges for each serial port, plus a high-current pad for the ESC harness.
parts.whyItMatters: Loose connectors cause more in-flight failures than chips do. Locking connectors cost more and are worth it.
buyingChecks: Ask whether the connectors are genuine JST-GH or a lookalike
Check each port's pinout matches your wiring
Check the ESC connector is rated for your telemetry and current

parts.name: Soft-mount grommets
parts.role: Isolate the board from frame vibration.
parts.whatItDoes: Four rubber grommets that sit in the mounting holes, so the board floats on rubber instead of bolting hard to the frame.
parts.whyItMatters: Vibration reaching the IMUs is the most common cause of a drone that drifts or oscillates. Grommet hardness matters.
buyingChecks: Ask for the grommet Shore hardness
Check the grommets fit M3 bolts without being crushed
Ask for spares: grommets harden with age

buyers: Drone makers building for defence and government tenders
demand.reason: Flight controllers are 80 to 90 percent imported in Indian drones, and China now licenses autopilot exports. Buyers who must show no Chinese parts need a traceable alternative.
